rule: Runbook criterion 11: every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict; no barrier is crossed with an open NOT DISCHARGED; and every 'behaviour the commit bodies do not mention' finding is either documented or reverted. R-35's mechanism was real and used throughout the campaign -- commit bodies across the range cite verify-P2b and verify-P5-retire findings and answer six NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts themselves were only ever written into commit bodies, so 'every slice has a recorded verdict' could not be checked from the repository. That is the first half of the criterion and it is the half this file exists to start.
what_this_ledger_does_not_hold: The verdicts of the campaign's earlier slices. They are recoverable only by reading the commit bodies that answer them, one range at a time, and reconstructing them here from those bodies would be this campaign's own failure shape -- a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. So the ledger starts where a lane could record a verdict honestly, which is the pass that produced it, and the gap for everything before it is stated rather than papered over. A campaign that ran this file from slice one would have the criterion; this one has the mechanism and one pass.

It returned that criterion unchanged and five further findings of behaviour the commit bodies do not mention -- two of them re-measurements of rows round 4 already carries, confirmed accurate rather than corrected, and one a confirmation that the three fixes round 4 cites are real in the tree and not merely narrated. What is new in this round is the structural half. criteria.what_was_found: Re-measured rather than read off round 4: git diff --stat 0248a42^..b19a577 -- src/ returns src/calculator/interpreters/__init__.py, 11 insertions / 10 deletions, and the same diff over 0248a42^..HEAD was identical when this round ran, so no commit had reverted it. 4876eb2 adds `from dataclasses import replace`, the module constant _CLOSEOUT and _AMP_WALK_LANE, and turns UnservedLane.retires_at into a per-lane conditional in two dict comprehensions plus three hand-spelled sites. Every mitigation round 4 lists is still true and none of them is what the criterion says. The verdict stands.
criteria.note: The cause is paid and the measurement still fails, and those are two different sentences. Paid: 8e36c60 removes retires_at from interpreters.UnservedLane entirely. src/ now declares the two facts about the tree a reader can check at import -- which interpreter produces the number, and by which lane -- and no stage at all; every unserved lane's retiring stage is resolved from the one stage record that declares itself the creditor_of that lane's debt, so a ruled re-dating is an edit to docs/receipts/campaign-stages.json alone. Measured after: git grep -n retires_at -- src/ returns nothing, against 6 occurrences before, and tests/test_behavior_frontier.py::test_no_campaign_stage_is_declared_anywhere_under_src asserts against source that no stage name any committed record declares appears anywhere under src/ and that UnservedLane's fields are exactly {reason, via}. Still failing: the criterion quantifies over four landed commits, and the only edit that would empty git diff 0248a42^..HEAD -- src/ is restoring the module to its 0248a42^ blob. That was considered and is refused for a reason and not for the cost. The blob dates the fourteen rows to 'Phase 4 S3 -- one kernel, five views', which Amendment K re-dated them OFF and Amendment F measured cannot perform the retiring act, so the runtime module would carry a superseded dating in the present tense; and because the gate binds the tree's declaration to the recorded stage, keeping it green would additionally take editing that clause. A false statement in src/, or a weakened gate, bought so that a measurement reads as a pass, is the ordering this campaign exists to invert -- the ledger's round-3 precedent refuses the same trade in the other direction, 'reverting a correct pin to satisfy an ownership sentence'. So the record is: the four commits changed src/, that is history and cannot be un-landed, and from 8e36c60 no future ruling can repeat it.

coverage.rule: Runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict -- had no denominator. 'Every slice' bounded nothing a machine could read, so a ledger holding one pass and a ledger holding forty were indistinguishable to every gate. This block is the denominator, derived from the tree rather than authored: the campaign's own slice labels, which are the trailing parenthetical tag each lane stamped on its commit subjects.
coverage.how_the_population_is_derived: The first element of the trailing parenthetical of every commit subject in 584071e..HEAD. A commit whose subject carries no such tag is counted in untagged_commits and reported rather than dropped -- a slice that never labelled itself is a hole in the convention, not an absence of slices.
coverage.what_this_block_does_not_do: It does not reconstruct a verdict. The earlier passes' verdicts live only in the commit bodies that answer them, and rebuilding them here from those bodies would be a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently -- the reason the ledger began mid-campaign. What is recorded is whether a slice group has a verdict IN THIS LEDGER, which is a fact about this file and is checkable without reading a single body. What it now DOES do is grade the residue instead of collapsing it: a slice group whose own commits record an R-35 verdict, naming the mechanism and carrying a verdict word, is listed by name under slice_groups_citing_a_verdict_in_a_commit_body (by name and not by sha: the ledger is committed inside the commit a sha would point at, so a sha here goes stale the moment that commit is amended). That is deliberately weaker than a recorded verdict -- a commit body is the LANE's transcription of the verifier's answer, not the verifier's artifact -- and it is a strict subset of the groups with none here, never a substitute. Collapsing 'a citation a reader can open' with 'nothing at all' is what made a ledger holding one pass and a ledger holding forty look alike to every gate.
coverage.what_the_residue_buys: Two things the criterion never had. The gap is a number that cannot grow in silence, the way the sole-home scan made criterion 4's residue a number. And the gate asserts the derived tag set equals these two lists -- so the NEXT slice group cannot ship without either a verdict row or an explicit line in slice_groups_without_one. Going forward the clause holds by machine; backwards it is measured and open, which is the honest pair. The forward half fired for real on 2026-08-15: the tag campaign-close-charge-price-oracle shipped with no line here, R-01 row 1 went red on the commit that shipped it, and the two rows were added by the next lane rather than discovered by a reader. That is the clause working, and it is recorded here because a gate whose one firing goes unrecorded is indistinguishable from a gate that has never fired.
coverage.why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroac: A verify verdict is a fresh read-only agent's report on a tree at a commit. The trees are still there and the agents are not, and a verdict written now by anyone who has read the plan is not an R-35 verdict at all -- the brief's whole content is that the reader has not read the plan. So the residue closes by the campaign ending, or by re-running R-35 over the historical ranges as its own scheduled work with its own briefs. It does not close by anybody filling in this file. Restated 2026-08-14 with the number: 10 of the groups without a verdict here cite one in a commit body, and the other rows cite nothing anywhere. Closing those is 60-odd fresh R-35 passes by verifiers that have not read the plan -- not a lane's to run, not reconstructible from the commit bodies of the lanes being checked, and not closeable by shrinking the denominator. It is recorded as an owed ruling in docs/receipts/rulings-owed.json rather than as a gap in a report. Prepared 2026-08-14: the branch that binds the clause backwards is now priced and startable row by row in docs/receipts/verify-backlog.json -- which changes what the ruling costs to schedule and changes nothing about the ruling, because preparing a pass is not running one.

a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_ci.raised_by: An R-35 residue-sweep pass over campaign-close-receipt-walk-r35, which returned that group's criterion-11 criterion NOT DISCHARGED against this file.
a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_ci.what_happened: ff9a488 is campaign-close-receipt-walk-r35's criterion-11 line. Its body states that a flag saying 'there is an answer about THIS group in a commit body' 'would be false, and it is measured false on the tree', and the body is deliberately worded to avoid the words the citation state is derived from. It was true when it was written. One commit later the same group's own 61f40a0 -- a gates performance commit whose body says 'No src/, no baseline, no counter moves' and mentions only verify-backlog.json -- added campaign-close-receipt-walk-r35 to slice_groups_citing_a_verdict_in_a_commit_body and moved residue_with_no_verdict_anywhere 78 -> 77 in this file, and its body does not mention this file at all. So at HEAD the ledger asserts the proposition ff9a488 recorded as measured false, and ff9a488's own criterion-11 line no longer describes the file it is a line about.
a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_ci.what_is_and_is_not_wrong: The derivation is right and stays untouched. tests/test_verify_ledger.py's _groups_citing_a_verdict_in_a_commit_body is a conjunction over a group's commit bodies -- a mechanism name AND a verdict word -- 61f40a0's body carries both, and the check is green and gated. What the derivation cannot do is tell WHOSE answer a body carries, and here it cannot: the answer 61f40a0 cites is an answer about campaign-close-receipt-walk-ruling, the group this one corrects, not about campaign-close-receipt-walk-r35. That limitation is already written into this block's own what_this_block_does_not_do -- the citation state is 'deliberately weaker than a recorded verdict' -- and this row is the first measured instance of it, recorded rather than repaired, because repairing it would mean widening a derived flag into an attribution nothing in a commit body supports.
a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_ci.why_it_is_recorded_here_and_not_argued_a: A group's criterion-11 line is a claim about this file, and a claim about a file that the file contradicts is the failure shape the whole ledger exists to catch -- it does not stop being one because the contradiction arrived from the group's own next commit. Neither body can be edited. So the record lands in the block the claim was about, where the next reader of either counter already is. Nothing in the coverage lists or counters moves on this account: 61f40a0's edit was correct arithmetic and stays exactly as it landed.
a_groups_own_next_commit_can_flip_its_ci.what_it_leaves_for_a_reader: Two things worth naming. A commit whose body declares 'no counter moves' moved a counter in this file, which is the same undeclared-change shape R-01's gate lines exist to prevent and is recorded here because that commit's body cannot be. And a group's citation flag is not stable across its own remaining commits: any later commit under the same tag can set it, so a criterion-11 line that asserts the flag's VALUE is asserting something its own group can still falsify, while one that states the group has no recorded verdict in this ledger cannot be.

prepared_work.what_it_holds: One row per group in slice_groups_without_one: the commits that group spans, by subject; the plan documents that carry its stated completion criteria; and whether its own commit bodies cite an R-35 answer. The brief is not copied into it -- it is read from R-35 in the runbook at run time, so a prepared pass can never be handed a weaker brief than the ruling states.
prepared_work.what_it_is_not: Coverage. Every row is a pass that has NOT run, and the backlog says so in its own words. It answers no part of the owed ruling and shrinks no denominator: its row set is asserted equal to this list, so preparing the work cannot become a way of redefining it.
prepared_work.why_it_exists: why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroactively says the residue closes by re-running R-35 over the historical ranges as scheduled work with its own briefs. No range and no brief existed anywhere in the tree, so the backwards branch of the owed ruling had a cost nobody could price beyond 'sixty-odd passes' and work nobody could begin. It now has one row per pass.

coverage.how_the_residue_was_measured_backwards: On 2026-08-17 the campaign's rendered R-35 verdicts were transcribed out of the orchestration journals into `passes` -- see the `backfill` block. What is left in slice_groups_without_one is the true residue of the first clause: slice tags no verifier's commit range ever reached. The clause is no longer measured against a ledger that started mid-campaign; it is measured against every verdict the campaign actually rendered.

vocabulary_notes.PHASE_TIP_ONLY: A third status the campaign's verifiers used and returned: a criterion stated over a phase tip, which the slice's own tip cannot decide. It is recorded as they wrote it. Folding it into DISCHARGED or NOT_DISCHARGED would be this ledger inventing a verdict rather than transcribing one.
vocabulary_notes.no_action_required: The disposition of a DISCHARGED row. The other four terms all describe what a lane did about a finding; a discharged criterion leaves no finding to do anything about, and before the backfill the ledger held only NOT_DISCHARGED rows, so the closed set had never needed the term.

backfill.what_it_is: Criterion 11's first clause, discharged backwards as far as the evidence reaches. The campaign's R-35 verdicts were rendered by fresh read-only Opus 5 verifiers with per-criterion evidence, and every one of them was recorded in the orchestration journal that spawned it -- one JSON line per agent result. Those verdicts are what this backfill transcribes. They are admissible for exactly the reason the ledger's own residue note gives for refusing a reconstruction: they are the verifiers' artifacts, not a later reader's account of a commit body.

source.shape: One JSON line per agent result. A verifier's line carries all_discharged, criteria[] (id, status, evidence) and unmentioned_behaviour[]. The brief it was handed -- R-35's, including 'Do not read the implementation plan' -- is the first line of the agent's own transcript file beside the journal.
source.how_a_verdict_was_joined_to_a_slice_tag: By commit, never by name. Each verifier's brief names the commits it verified; each commit's subject carries the trailing slice tag the coverage block derives its population from. A tag is covered when a verifier verified a commit that carries it. The verifiers' own labels ('P3-mig-r5', 'RW-swing-terms') are orchestration names and are kept only as provenance.

backfill.what_a_backfilled_row_claims: That this verdict was rendered, on these commits, by that verifier, and is transcribed rather than reconstructed. Evidence strings are clipped to 320 characters; the journal holds them whole.
backfill.what_it_does_not_claim: That anything answered the row. A backfilled block's `answered_by` names the slice group's own closing commit and its criterion rows carry an empty `answered_at`, because a verdict recorded after the fact has no answering commit -- the ledger's schema requires the field and this is what it honestly holds. Nor does it claim a NOT_DISCHARGED row is closed: those rows are documented, which is the disposition the third clause names, and no lane action is asserted.
backfill.why_this_is_not_the_reconstruction_the_l: `what_this_ledger_does_not_hold` refuses verdicts rebuilt out of the commit bodies that answer them -- a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. Nothing here is derived from a commit body. The verdicts are the verifiers' returned reports, held outside the repository, written before the commits that answered them, by readers who had not read the plan.
backfill.what_the_residue_still_holds: Slice tags no verifier's commit range reached. They are enumerated in slice_groups_without_one and prepared, one startable row each, in verify-backlog.json.

residue_sweep.what_it_is: The residue of criterion 11's first clause, closed forwards instead of backwards: R-35 re-run today over slice groups that landed earlier in the campaign and never had a verdict, each pass handed the slice's own commit range and R-35's brief read from the runbook. This is the route the ledger's own `why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroactively` names as the only one that closes a residue row -- 're-running R-35 over the historical ranges as its own scheduled work with its own briefs' -- and it is what verify-backlog.json prepares.
residue_sweep.how_it_differs_from_the_backfill: The backfill transcribed verdicts rendered DURING the campaign, at the tip each slice was verified against. A sweep pass is rendered NOW, against HEAD, over a commit that landed long ago. That is why its PHASE_TIP_ONLY rows read the way they do: the criterion's declared per-tip readings are unreproducible once later commits re-captured a baseline, and the verifier says so rather than substituting a number it could not measure.
residue_sweep.what_a_sweep_row_claims: That this verdict was rendered on this commit by that agent, and is transcribed rather than reconstructed. Evidence strings are clipped to 320 characters; the journal holds them whole.
residue_sweep.what_it_does_not_claim: That anything answered the row. A sweep block's `answered_by` names the slice's own commit and its rows carry an empty `answered_at`, because a verdict rendered after that commit landed has no answering commit -- the schema requires the field and this is what it honestly holds. Nor is a NOT_DISCHARGED row closed by being recorded: it is documented, which is the disposition the third clause names, and no lane action is asserted.

source.shape: One JSON line per agent result, carrying all_discharged, criteria[] (id, status, evidence) and unmentioned_behaviour[]. The brief the agent was handed -- R-35's, including 'Do not read the implementation plan' -- is the first line of the agent's own transcript file beside the journal, and it is what names the commit range each slice was verified over.
source.why_the_journal_and_not_the_handoff: The lane that records a batch is handed the verdicts in its own task text, which is truncated to fit. The journal line is the verifier's artifact, complete, and it is what was transcribed -- the recording lane may not be the reason a verdict goes missing.

residue_sweep.when_a_later_lane_answers_a_sweep_row: Added 2026-08-17. `what_it_does_not_claim` says a NOT_DISCHARGED sweep row is documented and that no lane action is asserted. That is what a RECORDING lane may claim; it is not a rule that the row can never be answered. When a later lane does act, the row records what acted -- `answered_at` names the commit, `disposition` moves off documented_open, and `note` says what was measured. The verdict itself is never re-graded, because a verdict is the verifier's artifact and a disposition is the lane's. Without this sentence the two halves read as a contradiction, and the ledger would be teaching that a sweep row is unanswerable by construction, which the block never meant.
